::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 25 [1899]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/82
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd) 
Here is a behind the times letter that concerns you.  I have heard from [Mr Thring](people/person_1281.qmd), who says I can remove my books with proper notice, but as I don’t know how long proper notice is, I have written to ask, also he thinks there may be trouble about those of which [A D I](people/person_744.qmd) gives Royalty and on the older ones there is no agreement.[^1]  I asked if I ought to wait to write to [Macmillan](organizations/other_111.qmd) till there is some decision about A D I

I don’t think, on considering it, that [FMP](people/person_1160.qmd)’s opinion goes for much, she has gone too much out of the range of English life.  I doubt [Skeffington](organizations/other_110.qmd) since the father died, he has been very ritualistic and also silly and sensational and I should question if he had extensive connection enough.  [Darton](organizations/other_109.qmd), if he has a soul for it would be better, and I am sure it is safer to be a mere publisher of principle and good taste and not an aspirant author which was one mistake.

Yes from 18 to 30 is the age to write for, but with a certain view to what might be good or bad for the younger ones who would read also.  [FMP](people/person_1160.qmd) has been staying in Scotland and with [Lady Macclesfield](people/person_1655.qmd), also [Miss Acland](people/person_8.qmd) /Oxford\\, so she has been seeing varieties.  I shall have [Annie Moberly](people/person_1024.qmd) for a week in September and she is of much use to talk to, though too busy to be any good when her term begins.  I did not like to ask FMP point blank, but I doubt her having read [the Long Vacation](cmy_books/cmybook_237.qmd) where I think Emilia, Gillian and Dolores are all essentially modern young ladies. <sup>2</sup>

The glass is really going down but there is hardly a blade of grass left except under the trees and in the water meadows.  Yarrow and plantain, also thistles do what they can

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: George Herbert Thring (1859-1941), solicitor, Secretary of the [Society of Authors](organizations/other_44.qmd), 1891-1906.  He was the son of Edward Thring, the headmaster of Uppingham whose book on teaching CMY so admired.
